items.stem: What is the y-intercept of y = 3 × 2ˣ?
Explain why y = 2ˣ is always positive.
items.answer: A positive number raised to any real power is positive, so the graph stays above the x-axis.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: A positive number raised to any real power is positive, so the graph stays above the x-axis. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: "y = 2ˣ crosses the x-axis at x = 0." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: It never crosses the x-axis; it crosses the y-axis at (0, 1).
items.markingKey: It never crosses the x-axis; it crosses the y-axis at (0, 1). 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: For y = −(1/3)ˣ + 5: (a) find the y-intercept, (b) state the horizontal asymptote, (c) state whether the function is increasing or decreasing, (d) state the range.
items.answer: (a) (0, 4) (b) y = 5 (c) increasing (d) y < 5
items.markingKey: y-intercept (A1); asymptote (A1); increasing – check values f(−1) = 2, f(1) = 14/3, f(2) = 44/9 (A1); range (A1).

items.stem: The graph of y = a × 2ˣ + c has horizontal asymptote y = −1 and passes through (0, 0). Find a and c, and hence find y when x = 1.
items.markingKey: c from the asymptote (A1); a + c = 0 → a = 1 (A1); y = 1 × 2¹ − 1 = 1 (A1).

items.stem: A cup of coffee in a café in Seoul cools according to T(t) = 20 + 65 × 0.85ᵗ °C after t minutes. (a) Find the initial temperature. (b) Find the temperature after 10 minutes. (c) State the horizontal asymptote and interpret it. (d) After how many whole minutes is the coffee first below 40 °C?
items.answer: (a) T(0) = 85 °C (b) T(10) = 32.8 °C (c) y = 20: the coffee cools towards room temperature (d) about 8 minutes
items.markingKey: (a) T(0) = 85 °C (b) T(10) = 32.8 °C (c) y = 20: the coffee cools towards room temperature (d) about 8 minutes. Exponential features found (A1 A1); calculations (M1 A1); pattern / limitation explained (B/D: R1).

items.stem: State what is meant by the term "exponential function".
items.answer: A function of the form f(x) = a × bˣ + c with b > 0, b ≠ 1
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: a function of the form f(x) = a × bˣ + c with b > 0, b ≠ 1. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "horizontal asymptote"?
options: The difference between an observed value and the value predicted by a model
If successive y-values (for equal x-steps) have an approximately constant ratio, an exponential model is suitable
The line y = c that the graph of y = a × bˣ + c approaches but never reaches
The behaviour of y = bˣ, which increases (growth) when b > 1 and decreases (decay) when 0 < b < 1
items.answer: The line y = c that the graph of y = a × bˣ + c approaches but never reaches
items.markingKey: C. "horizontal asymptote" is the line y = c that the graph of y = a × bˣ + c approaches but never reaches.

items.stem: Ingrid says y = 4ˣ + 4 crosses the x-axis when x is very negative. Explain why this is wrong.
items.answer: 4ˣ > 0 for all x, so y > 4 > 0; the graph approaches the asymptote y = 4 but never crosses the x-axis.
items.markingKey: Positivity (R1); asymptote (R1).

items.stem: Maya writes: "y = (1/2)ˣ is the same as y = −2ˣ." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: (1/2)ˣ = 2^(−x), a reflection in the y-axis, and is positive; −2ˣ is negative.
items.markingKey: (1/2)ˣ = 2^(−x), a reflection in the y-axis, and is positive; −2ˣ is negative. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why y = 2ˣ eventually becomes larger than y = x² + 40, even though it is smaller at x = 5.
items.answer: 2ˣ doubles each time x increases by 1, while a quadratic grows by a steadily increasing but additive amount; exponential growth always overtakes polynomial growth (e.g. at x = 10: 1024 vs 140).
items.markingKey: Growth comparison (R1); numerical evidence (A1).

items.stem: Explain why every graph y = bˣ passes through (0, 1).
items.answer: b⁰ = 1 for any b > 0.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: b⁰ = 1 for any b > 0. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: For y = −4ˣ + 2: (a) find the y-intercept, (b) state the horizontal asymptote, (c) state whether the function is increasing or decreasing, (d) state the range.
items.answer: (a) (0, 1) (b) y = 2 (c) decreasing (d) y < 2
items.markingKey: y-intercept (A1); asymptote (A1); decreasing – check values f(−1) = 7/4, f(1) = −2, f(2) = −14 (A1); range (A1).

items.stem: The graph of y = a × 4ˣ + c has horizontal asymptote y = 3 and passes through (0, 4). Find a and c, and hence find y when x = 2.
items.markingKey: c from the asymptote (A1); a + c = 4 → a = 1 (A1); y = 1 × 4² + 3 = 19 (A1).

items.stem: The graph of y = a × 3ˣ + c has horizontal asymptote y = 5 and passes through (0, 9). Find a and c, and hence find y when x = 3.
items.markingKey: c from the asymptote (A1); a + c = 9 → a = 4 (A1); y = 4 × 3³ + 5 = 113 (A1).

items.stem: For y = 3 × 4ˣ + 4: (a) find the y-intercept, (b) state the horizontal asymptote, (c) state whether the function is increasing or decreasing, (d) state the range.

items.markingKey: y-intercept (A1); asymptote (A1); increasing – check values f(−1) = 19/4, f(1) = 16, f(2) = 52 (A1); range (A1).

items.stem: A savings app in Lisbon offers Plan A: 500 points plus 80 points per day, or Plan B: 2ⁿ points on day n. (a) Write a formula for each plan. (b) Compare the points after 5 days. (c) On which day does Plan B first give more points? (d) Explain why this always happens eventually.
items.answer: (a) Plan A: 500 + 80n; Plan B: 2ⁿ (b) after 5 days A gives 900, B gives 32 (c) day 11 (d) exponential growth eventually overtakes linear growth
items.markingKey: (a) Plan A: 500 + 80n; Plan B: 2ⁿ (b) after 5 days A gives 900, B gives 32 (c) day 11 (d) exponential growth eventually overtakes linear growth. Exponential features found (A1 A1); calculations (M1 A1); pattern / limitation explained (B/D: R1).

items.stem: A rumour spreads in a school in Lima: 3 students know it on day 0, and the number multiplies by 1.5 each day. (a) Find the numbers on days 0, 1 and 2. (b) Write a model N(t). (c) On which day does N first reach 1,000? (d) Explain why the model fails eventually.

items.stem: Explain why a town growing by 20% a year gains more people each year, while one growing by 500 people a year does not.
items.answer: 20% of a larger population is a larger number each year (exponential), whereas adding 500 is the same every year (linear).
items.markingKey: Percentage of a changing amount (R1); comparison (R1).

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why the half-life does not depend on the starting amount.
items.answer: N₀(1/2)^(t/h) halves whenever t increases by h, whatever N₀ is. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)
items.markingKey: Award marks for: N₀(1/2)^(t/h) halves whenever t increases by h, whatever N₀ is. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.) (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: An exponential model y = a × bˣ passes through (1, 3/2) and (2, 3/4). Find a and b.
Aiko writes: "After two half-lives nothing is left." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: A quarter is left; each half-life halves what remains.

items.stem: The graph of y = a × 3ˣ + c has horizontal asymptote y = −4 and passes through (0, 1). Find a and c, and hence find y when x = 2.
items.markingKey: c from the asymptote (A1); a + c = 1 → a = 5 (A1); y = 5 × 3² − 4 = 41 (A1).

items.stem: The visitors to a website (hundreds) in Lisbon over 5 days (day 0 to day 4) were 196, 240, 287, 342, 414. (a) Show that the data are approximately exponential. (b) Estimate the ratio b and write a model y = a × bᵗ. (c) Predict day 7.

items.stem: A student in Dubai drinks coffee with 120 mg of caffeine; caffeine has a half-life of about 6 hours. (a) Write a model for the caffeine C mg after t hours. (b) Find the amount after 8 hours. (c) After how many whole hours is it first below 20 mg? (d) Explain when the caffeine leaves the body fastest.
items.answer: (a) C = 120(1/2)^(t/6) (b) 47.6 mg (c) about 16 hours (d) the decay is fastest at first in mg per hour, because half of a larger amount is lost each half-life

items.stem: Investigate the family y = bˣ + 4 for b = 2, 3 and 5. (a) Find the y-intercept and asymptote of each. (b) Describe how the value of b changes the graph. (c) State the point common to all the graphs. (d) Predict what happens when 0 < b < 1.
items.answer: (a) y-intercepts 1 + 4 = 5 for all; asymptote y = 4 (b) larger b is steeper for x > 0 and flatter for x < 0 (c) they all meet at (0, 5) (d) b between 0 and 1 gives decreasing graphs with the same asymptote

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "doubling time"?
options: If successive y-values (for equal x-steps) have an approximately constant ratio, an exponential model is suitable
The time taken for a growing quantity to double
N(t) = N₀ × bᵗ with b > 1, or N(t) = N₀(1 + r)ᵗ for growth at rate r per period
The time taken for a decaying quantity to halve
items.answer: The time taken for a growing quantity to double
items.markingKey: B. "doubling time" is the time taken for a growing quantity to double.

items.stem: State the y-intercept and horizontal asymptote of y = 4 × 2ˣ + 4.

items.answer: exponential regression
items.markingKey: D. This is the definition of exponential regression.

items.stem: Explain why exponential decay never reaches zero in the model.
items.answer: Each period the amount is multiplied by a positive number less than 1, so it stays positive.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Each period the amount is multiplied by a positive number less than 1, so it stays positive. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain why y = 2ˣ eventually becomes larger than y = x² + 80, even though it is smaller at x = 4.
items.answer: 2ˣ doubles each time x increases by 1, while a quadratic grows by a steadily increasing but additive amount; exponential growth always overtakes polynomial growth (e.g. at x = 10: 1024 vs 180).
items.markingKey: Growth comparison (R1); numerical evidence (A1).

items.stem: Mei says the data 8, 10, 12, 14 (for x = 0, 1, 2, 3) are exponential. Explain why a linear model is better.
items.answer: The differences are all 2 (constant), while the ratios 1.25, 1.20, 1.17 are not constant.
items.markingKey: Differences (A1); ratios not constant (R1).

items.stem: A medicine has a half-life of 5 hours. Mateo says it will all be gone after 10 hours. Explain why this is wrong.
items.answer: Each half-life halves what remains: after 5 h, 1/2 is left; after 10 h, 1/4 is left.
items.markingKey: Repeated halving (R1); fraction left (A1).

items.stem: "y = (1/2)ˣ is the same as y = −2ˣ." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: (1/2)ˣ = 2^(−x), a reflection in the y-axis, and is positive; −2ˣ is negative.
items.markingKey: (1/2)ˣ = 2^(−x), a reflection in the y-axis, and is positive; −2ˣ is negative. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why the differences of 5, 15, 45, 135 are not constant, but the data still follow a simple pattern.
items.answer: Differences 10, 30, 90 grow, but each term is 3 times the last: a constant ratio, so y = 5 × 3ˣ.
items.markingKey: Ratio identified (R1); model (A1).
